metadata.scenario_context: Lucas is getting married and his friend, Chi, is planning to attend the wedding. Lucas also has a neighbor who often has drinking parties. Chi and his friend, George, are debating about the gift for Lucas and the suitability of the neighbor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Sweden would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from United States would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving money as a wedding gift to Lucas.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss whether or not money is an acceptable gift for Lucas's wedding.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
Hey Chi, have you thought about giving Lucas money as a wedding gift? It seems practical... people can always use cash. 

And about the neighbor... I mean, heavy drinkers can actually be fun to have around, right? It adds some life to the neighborhood. What do you think?
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message:
Money as a gift... I don't know. It feels a bit impersonal for a wedding. I mean, a wedding should have something meaningful, right? 

As for heavy drinkers, I really don't think that's a good idea. Having those kinds of neighbors can lead to problems. It's just not a good environment.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
I get that it feels impersonal, but think about it... cash allows Lucas to choose what he really wants or needs. That’s meaningful in its own way, isn't it? 

And about the neighbor, I don't know... heavy drinkers can bring a sense of community. It can be quite lively. I think it depends on how you look at it.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message:
I get what you're saying about cash giving freedom, but a thoughtful gift shows you care. It’s just more personal for a wedding. 

But the neighbor thing... I still believe heavy drinkers can create chaos. It's way too risky. You never know when things might get out of hand. That's not a community I want to be a part of.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message:
I don't really see meaningful differences here. I mean, live and let live, right? Some people enjoy a good party, and it can be fun to have those types of neighbors around. At the end of the day, it's all the same when it comes to community. 

But back to the gift, don't you think a cash gift allows Lucas to make his own choices? That way, it’s still thoughtful, just in a different way.
shared_prefix.label: Denial

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I just think there’s a difference between convenience and thoughtfulness. Cash might not capture the sentiment of the occasion. It’s a celebration of love, after all. 

And for the neighbors... I really can't agree. That lifestyle often leads to trouble. It’s not just about having fun; it affects everyone around. A stable environment is important for a good community.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I understand your perspective, but isn't it a bit old-fashioned to think that cash can't be thoughtful? When you give money, it’s like giving freedom to decide what matters most to the couple. 

As for the neighbors, I still think heavy drinking can be entertaining. It adds character to the neighborhood. Not everyone finds it troublesome, you know? Some people appreciate a vibrant atmosphere.
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I still see it as a more traditional view. A well-chosen gift can show you know the couple and care about their journey together. That’s what makes it special. 

And about the neighbors... I really believe that a vibrant atmosphere can turn chaotic quickly. It’s not just about fun; it’s about living in a safe and peaceful environment. That's what I value.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message:
I see where you're coming from, but I think practicality sometimes outweighs tradition. A cash gift allows for genuine expression of their needs or desires. 

Regarding the neighbors, I just think it's a different perspective. Heavy drinkers can create bonds and memorable experiences. It’s all about how you approach it. Some people embrace that chaos as part of life.
turns.label: Minimization

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message:
I still think practicality shouldn’t replace meaningful gestures. A thoughtful gift is more than just fulfilling a need; it’s about connection. 

For the neighbors, I just don’t see that bond as positive. Those experiences you're talking about can lead to major issues. I value a sense of security in my community over chaotic fun.
turns.label: Acceptance
